# Capability

Capability is an open experimental standard, runtime, CLI, developer kit, and federated discovery network for executable abilities that software agents can discover before installation, inspect before execution, authorize by declared effects, acquire with provenance checks, run through isolation, verify, and receipt.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/wheresmycoleslaw/capability
npm package: @wheresmycoleslaw/capability
Public documentation: https://sithix.com/capability
Default index: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wheresmycoleslaw/capability/main/registry/index.json

## Bootstrap an MCP host

Run:

npx -y @wheresmycoleslaw/capability mcp-serve

The bridge exposes five stable MCP tools:
- capability_search: discover abilities on demand
- capability_inspect: inspect inert contracts and declared effects
- capability_execute: verified acquisition and isolated execution
- capability_probe_site: discover indexes advertised by a website
- capability_doctor: local/network readiness check

The MCP bridge supports modern MCP server/discover negotiation and the legacy initialize flow for compatibility.

## Discover a website

Participating websites advertise a JSON discovery document at:
- /.well-known/capabilities
- /.well-known/capabilities.json

The document points to one or more Capability indexes and may advertise an MCP bootstrap endpoint or package. The document is a locator, not a trust root.

CLI:
cap probe https://example.com

## Discover abilities

cap find "desired outcome"
cap info capability/id
cap exec capability/id '{"input":"value"}' --executor=auto

Capability indexes are inert discovery metadata. The client still verifies the exact executable package and manifest binding before execution.

## Build an ability

npx @wheresmycoleslaw/capability create my-capability --id my-domain/my-ability
cd my-capability
npm install
npm test
npm run readiness
npm run novelty

## Key design distinction

MCP answers how an agent communicates with tools. Capability focuses on how an agent discovers an ability it was not prewired with, inspects it, resolves an exact implementation, verifies/acquires it, authorizes its effects, executes it in isolation, and records a receipt.
